In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the radiation hardness of components and systems for the optical link of the ATLAS detector.
the development of radiation hard components for the ATLAS liquid Argon Calorimeter front end electronics.
the development of a radiation-hard optical link for use in the ATLAS detector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all the optical components (VCSEL's, optical fibres and PIN-photodiode receivers) are radiation-hard.
all components have been shown to be radiation hard.
, in the current design, the optical link components can survive the ATLAS radiation environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optical links developed for use in the front-end electronics of the ATLAS calorimeter are radiation tolerant to the levels of radiation expected during the lifetime of the experiment.
all of the tested components of the link are able to withstand the radiation levels foreseen for ATLAS.
the radiation effects are small and can be neglected for the link design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiation tolerance of VCSEL's is sufficient to allow them to operate for the duration of the ATLAS data-taking.
